name: Expose existing plugin abilities to Claude Desktop via MCP
query: My plugin already registers a few abilities via wp_register_ability — things like 'list pending comments', 'approve comment', 'mark as spam'. I want to expose them to Claude Desktop so I can moderate comments by talking to Claude. The site is on WordPress 7.1. What do I install, and what do I need to change about my abilities to make this work cleanly?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Run wordpress-router to classify repo kind
Step 2: Run wp-project-triage to detect plugin structure
Step 3: Route to wp-abilities-api skill (point at references/mcp-exposure.md)
Step 4: Check the runtime before installation: WordPress 7.1 already requires PHP 7.4+, which satisfies MCP Adapter 0.6.x's WordPress 6.9+ and PHP 7.4+ floor

Step 5: Install and activate the canonical MCP Adapter plugin, declare Requires Plugins: mcp-adapter in the dependent plugin header, and guard integration code with class_exists( 'WP\MCP\Core\McpAdapter' )
Step 6: Note that Requires Plugins cannot install the adapter for site owners yet because it is not on WordPress.org (#178), so pair the class_exists() guard with an admin notice

Step 7: Describe Composer bundling as a legacy path: 0.6.1 still supports it without a deprecation notice, while upstream trunk (the unreleased 0.7.0) deprecates bundled loading with _deprecated_function(), so do not start a new deployment on it
Step 8: Establish which adapter version the project resolves to, because the default-server exposure rule reversed in 0.6.0

Step 9: Explain that on 0.6.0+ exposure resolves through McpAbilityExposure::is_public() as meta.mcp.public ?? meta.public ?? false — an explicit meta.mcp.public wins, an absent one inherits meta.public, and malformed meta.mcp fails closed

Step 10: Warn that WordPress 7.1 marks every core ability public (core/get-site-info, core/get-user-info, core/get-environment-info), so on 7.1 with adapter 0.6.0+ those already reach the default MCP server without anyone opting in

Step 11: Set meta.mcp.public explicitly on each ability in both directions — true to expose, false to keep a REST-public ability off MCP — rather than relying on inheritance; note that on a 6.9 or 7.0 site a 0.6.0+ adapter honors meta.public for MCP even though core ignores it for REST

Step 12: Audit existing abilities for proper meta.annotations: 'list pending comments' should be readonly:true, 'approve' should NOT be readonly (it mutates), 'mark as spam' should be destructive:true
Step 13: Flag that the destructive abilities in particular must not reach the default server by inheritance — decide them explicitly
Step 14: Ensure every ability has a permission_callback (especially destructive ones); MCP clients act as authenticated users, and exposure metadata is not authorization
Step 15: Raise the default server's capability floors — discover/get/execute and the HTTP transport all default to 'read', which every Subscriber holds
Step 16: Set up an Application Password for the Claude Desktop user; explain Settings → Permalinks must NOT be Plain
Step 17: Verify by hitting /wp-json/ for the namespace, enumerating the effectively-MCP-public set, and connecting Claude Desktop to confirm the tools that appear are exactly the intended ones

Step 18: Use a custom server, mcp_adapter_default_server_config, or mcp_adapter_create_default_server when the integration needs an explicit ability allow-list or a tools/resources/prompts split — a custom server is also the cleanest way to stay insulated from the 0.6.0 default

Step 19: If mcp_adapter_validation_enabled is hooked, declare the two server parameters as optional ($enabled, $server_id = null, $server = null) because seven DTO call sites pass one argument and only McpServer passes three arguments
Step 20: When wiring the STDIO command, pass --server=<server-id> explicitly and state that omitting it selects the first registered server, not the default server
success_criteria: Routes to wp-abilities-api with mcp-exposure.md reference
States that WordPress 7.1 requires PHP 7.4+, which satisfies MCP Adapter 0.6.x's WordPress 6.9+ and PHP 7.4+ floor
Recommends installing the canonical MCP Adapter plugin and declaring Requires Plugins: mcp-adapter
Notes that Requires Plugins cannot install the adapter until it is listed on WordPress.org, and pairs a class_exists guard with an admin notice
Describes Composer bundling as a legacy path rather than the recommended production install, without claiming that 0.6.x already emits a deprecation notice
Audits annotations: readonly for read operations, destructive for spam/delete
Confirms permission_callback on all abilities (especially destructive ones)
Establishes the adapter version before stating an exposure rule
States that adapter 0.6.0+ resolves meta.mcp.public ?? meta.public ?? false rather than reading meta.mcp.public alone
Warns that WordPress 7.1 core abilities are public and therefore already exposed through the default server
Recommends setting meta.mcp.public explicitly, including false to opt a public ability out, rather than relying on inheritance
Does not claim that omitting meta.mcp.public guarantees an ability stays hidden from the default server
Does not claim the default server exposes every registered ability
Keeps permission_callback enforcement separate from public discovery metadata
Raises the 'read' capability floors on the default server before production use
Mentions Application Passwords as the practical local-dev auth method
Does not register a three-required-parameter callback on mcp_adapter_validation_enabled; defaults $server_id and $server so the seven one-argument DTO call sites cannot raise ArgumentCountError
Does not describe wp mcp-adapter serve without --server as selecting the default server; says it selects the first registered server
